questions.question: Let $h_1,\dots,h_N$ be differentiable quasi-convex on an open convex $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in D\colon h_k(\boldsymbol{x})\leq0\ \forall k\}$, $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$. The cone $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ used for supporting hyperplanes from gradients consists of all vectors $\sum_{k=1}^{N}\lambda_k\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_k(\boldsymbol{p})$ whose coefficients satisfy which conditions?
options: $\lambda_k\in\mathbb{R}$ of any sign when $h_k(\boldsymbol{p})=0$, and $\lambda_k=0$ otherwise

questions.question: Let $h_1,\dots,h_N$ be differentiable quasi-convex functions on an open convex $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in D\colon h_k(\boldsymbol{x})\leq0\ \forall k\}$, $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$, and $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ the cone generated by the $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_k(\boldsymbol{p})$ with $h_k(\boldsymbol{p})=0$. If $h_k(\boldsymbol{p})<0$ for every $k$, what is $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$?
options: $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$, so the gradients give no supporting hyperplane of $V$ through $\boldsymbol{p}$
$C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ is the cone generated by all $N$ gradients $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_k(\boldsymbol{p})$, as none of them is excluded
$C_{\boldsymbol{p}}=\varnothing$, because there is no active gradient that could be combined
$C_{\boldsymbol{p}}=\mathbb{R}^n$, because every direction from $\boldsymbol{p}$ stays inside $V$ for small steps

questions.question: Let $h_1,\dots,h_N$ be differentiable quasi-convex on an open convex $D$, $V=\{h_k\leq0\ \forall k\}$, $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$, and $\boldsymbol{a}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$ a nonnegative combination of active gradients $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_k(\boldsymbol{p})$. Where does $V$ always lie relative to $H_{\boldsymbol{a}}=\{\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}\}$?
options: In $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}$, as each active gradient points into $V$
In $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}$, as each active gradient points out of $V$
In $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}<\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}$ for every $\boldsymbol{x}\in V\setminus\{\boldsymbol{p}\}$, so $H_{\boldsymbol{a}}$ meets $V$ only at $\boldsymbol{p}$

questions.question: For $V=\{h_k\leq0\ \forall k\}$ with differentiable quasi-convex $h_k$ and $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$, supporting hyperplanes from gradients, $\{\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}\}$, use only $\boldsymbol{a}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$ in the cone $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ generated by the active gradients. Why is $\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{0}$ excluded?
options: Because $\boldsymbol{0}\notin C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$: a nonnegative combination of gradients cannot be the zero vector
Because $\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{0}$ arises only at interior points of $V$, where no hyperplane can support $V$
Because for $\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{0}$ the inequality $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}$ fails for some $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$
Because $\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{0}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=0\}$ is all of $\mathbb{R}^n$, which is not a hyperplane

questions.question: Let $V=\{h_i\leq0\ \forall i\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty, with affine $h_i(\boldsymbol{x})=\boldsymbol{a}_i^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}-b_i$, $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$, and $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ the cone generated by the active $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_i(\boldsymbol{p})$. What are these gradients, and how does $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ compare with the normal cone $N_V(\boldsymbol{p})$?
options: $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_i(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{a}_i$, but $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ is a proper subset of $N_V(\boldsymbol{p})$ where two or more rows are active
$\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_i(\boldsymbol{p})=-\boldsymbol{a}_i$, since the gradient points into the polyhedral set $V$
$\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_i(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{a}_i$, and $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}=N_V(\boldsymbol{p})$ at every point $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$
$\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_i(\boldsymbol{p})=\boldsymbol{a}_i$, and $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}=N_V(\boldsymbol{p})$ only where one constraint is active

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+2x_2\leq8,\ 3x_1-x_2\leq3,\ x_2\leq5\}$, written with $h_1=x_1+2x_2-8$, $h_2=3x_1-x_2-3$, $h_3=x_2-5$, and let $\boldsymbol{p}=(2,3)$. Which set is the cone $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ of nonnegative combinations of the active gradients at $\boldsymbol{p}$?

Let $h(\boldsymbol{x})=x_1^2+3x_2^2-7$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ (convex and differentiable), $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon h(\boldsymbol{x})\leq0\}$ and $\boldsymbol{p}=(2,1)$, where $h(\boldsymbol{p})=0$. Which inequality for all $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$ does the supporting hyperplane with normal $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h(\boldsymbol{p})$ give?

Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon h_1(\boldsymbol{x})\leq0,\ h_2(\boldsymbol{x})\leq0\}$ with $h_1=x_1^2+x_2^2-25$ and $h_2=x_2-3$, and let $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ be the cone of nonnegative combinations of the gradients of the constraints active at $\boldsymbol{p}$. At which point $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$ is $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$?

On $D=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1>0,\ x_2>0\}$ let $h(\boldsymbol{x})=4-x_1x_2$ (quasi-convex, differentiable), $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in D\colon h(\boldsymbol{x})\leq0\}$ and $\boldsymbol{p}=(1,4)$. Which half-plane containing $V$, bounded by a supporting line through $\boldsymbol{p}$, does $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h(\boldsymbol{p})$ give?

The set $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_2\geq x_1^2+1\}$ is to be written as $\{h\leq0\}$ with a convex differentiable $h$, and the gradient at $\boldsymbol{p}=(2,5)$ is to give a supporting line. Which half-plane containing $V$, bounded by a line through $\boldsymbol{p}$, results?

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be open and convex, $h\colon D\to\mathbb{R}$ differentiable and quasi-convex, and $\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{p}\in D$ with $h(\boldsymbol{x})\leq h(\boldsymbol{p})$. Which inequality is guaranteed for all such $h$, $\boldsymbol{x}$ and $\boldsymbol{p}$?

options: $f(\boldsymbol{x})\leq f(\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast})$ for all $\boldsymbol{x}\in V$, whatever the shape of $f$

questions.question: Let $h_1,\dots,h_N$ be convex differentiable on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $V=\{h_k\leq0\ \forall k\}\neq\varnothing$, $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$, and $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ the cone generated by the $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_k(\boldsymbol{p})$ with $h_k(\boldsymbol{p})=0$. Which condition guarantees that every supporting hyperplane of $V$ through $\boldsymbol{p}$ has a normal in $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$?
options: Exactly one constraint $h_k$ is active at the point $\boldsymbol{p}$
Every $h_k$ is strictly convex on the whole of $\mathbb{R}^n$
The set $V$ is closed and bounded, hence compact

questions.question: For $f(\boldsymbol{x})=x_1^2+x_2^2$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$, the epigraph $\operatorname{Epi}(f)=\{(\boldsymbol{x},t)\in\mathbb{R}^3\colon h(\boldsymbol{x},t)\leq0\}$ with $h(\boldsymbol{x},t)=f(\boldsymbol{x})-t$. Which half-space containing $\operatorname{Epi}(f)$ does $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h$ at $\boldsymbol{p}=(1,2,5)$ give?

Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1^2+x_2^2\leq5,\ x_1+x_2\leq3\}$ and $\boldsymbol{p}=(2,1)$, where both constraints are active. Which half-plane bounded by a line through $\boldsymbol{p}$ is obtained from a vector of $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}\setminus\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and contains $V$?

Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1^2+4x_2^2\leq8\}$ and $\boldsymbol{p}=(2,1)$, a point of the boundary. Using the gradient of $h(\boldsymbol{x})=x_1^2+4x_2^2-8$ at $\boldsymbol{p}$, what is the greatest value of $x_1+2x_2$ on $V$?

Let $h_1,\dots,h_N$ be differentiable quasi-convex on open convex $D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, $V=\{h_k\leq0\ \forall k\}$, $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$, $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ the cone generated by the $\boldsymbol{\nabla} h_k(\boldsymbol{p})$ with $h_k(\boldsymbol{p})=0$, $\partial V$ its boundary. How are $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}\neq\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and $\boldsymbol{p}\in\partial V$ related in general?
options: $\boldsymbol{p}\in\partial V$ holds if and only if $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}\neq\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$
$C_{\boldsymbol{p}}\neq\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$ can hold at an interior point of $V$ where a constraint is active
$\boldsymbol{p}\in\partial V$ implies that every constraint is active at $\boldsymbol{p}$

questions.question: The closed unit disc $V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ is described once as $\{h\leq0\}$ with $h(\boldsymbol{x})=x_1^2+x_2^2-1$ and once as $\{g\leq0\}$ with $g(\boldsymbol{x})=(x_1^2+x_2^2-1)^3$; both are differentiable on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Which statement about the gradient cones $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ at $\boldsymbol{p}=(1,0)$ is correct?
options: Both descriptions give the ray $\{(s,0)\colon s\geq0\}$, as $C_{\boldsymbol{p}}$ depends only on $V$
$h$ gives the ray $\{(s,0)\colon s\geq0\}$, whereas $g$ gives only $\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$
$h$ gives the ray $\{(s,0)\colon s\geq0\}$; $g$ is not quasi-convex, so no cone arises
$h$ gives the ray $\{(s,0)\colon s\geq0\}$, whereas $g$ gives all of $\mathbb{R}^2$

questions.question: On $\mathbb{R}^2$ let $h(\boldsymbol{x})=x_2-x_1^2$ (not quasi-convex), $V=\{h\leq0\}$, $\boldsymbol{p}=(1,1)$ and $\boldsymbol{a}=\boldsymbol{\nabla} h(\boldsymbol{p})$. Applying the result on supporting hyperplanes from gradients anyway would claim $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{p}$ on $V$. Which point lies in $V$ and violates this claim?

Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon(x_1-1)^2+x_2^2\leq1,\ (x_1+1)^2+x_2^2\leq1\}=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$, two discs that touch at $\boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{0}$, and let $C_{\boldsymbol{0}}$ be the cone of nonnegative combinations of the active gradients at $\boldsymbol{0}$. Which statement is correct?
options: $C_{\boldsymbol{0}}=\{(s,0)\colon s\in\mathbb{R}\}$, and it contains the normal of every supporting line of $V$ through $\boldsymbol{0}$
$C_{\boldsymbol{0}}=\{\boldsymbol{0}\}$, because the gradients $(-2,0)$ and $(2,0)$ cancel each other
$C_{\boldsymbol{0}}=\mathbb{R}^2$, since two active constraints at a single point give every direction
